title: Shark Bay has about 4,800 square kilometres of seagrass beds
body: Western Australia's Shark Bay contains an extensive system of underwater seagrass meadows. These flowering plants are a food source for dugongs, the marine mammals sometimes called sea cows.
takeaway: A bay can have a vast productive landscape whose vegetation is hidden below the surface.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Shark Bay (1991)
visual: a dugong grazing above a broad underwater meadow

title: Three national parks meet in a single Congo Basin forest
body: The Sangha Trinational property joins adjoining parks in Cameroon, the Central African Republic and the Republic of the Congo. Together the parks protect about 7,500 square kilometres of largely intact forest.
takeaway: Connecting protected areas leaves room for forest animals to move beyond the limits of any one park.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sangha Trinational (2012)
visual: an unbroken canopy of Congo Basin forest split by a meandering river
